resolutions.capability: exact provider Message/Usage/Content schemas and serialization
resolutions.rationale: AI-019 explicitly owns the complete nested provider data contracts; AI-006 remains request-option authority.

resolutions.capability: SimpleStreamOptions and dynamic credential/provider routing
resolutions.rationale: The raw loop forwards the complete shared request option envelope, which AI-006 owns. Dynamic key resolution is the supplied getApiKey callback; default provider dispatch is AI-003. Do not make the callback seam depend on the coding-agent auth store or UI.

resolutions.capability: validateToolArguments schema/coercion and error contract
resolutions.rationale: Argument preparation then validateToolArguments requires the exact shared validator/coercion/error contract. The trusted beforeToolCall hook and no-revalidation behavior remain AGENT-012.

resolutions.capability: native host exposure of critical awaited loop callbacks
resolutions.rationale: The Agent SDK forwards low-level callbacks. Extension host binding, hook reducers and native event payload ownership consume those hooks; they are downstream integration references rather than build prerequisites of the Agent wrapper.

resolutions.capability: parseStreamingJson partial JSON repair contract
resolutions.rationale: Proxy partial tool JSON calls parseStreamingJson. AI-011 specifies repair order, permissive runtime root types and failure fallback; execution-time validation is separate.

resolutions.capability: working Rust AgentHarness, durable Session storage, lanes and operation recovery
resolutions.rationale: This TS export is a scaffold that rejects operations, while Rust already has a working AgentHarness. Session branch/lane/log recovery entries document preserved native behavior. No new harness implementation dependency should be inferred from the scaffold.

resolutions.capability: foreground tool wrapper output capture/truncation and durable background-shell ownership
resolutions.rationale: The execution environment drains pipes and emits chunks. The capture wrappers and background registry consume it, and TOOLS-010/015 already depend on AGENT-050. The original phrase 'durable background-shell ownership' is inaccurate: the registry is in memory; only logs/branch notifications are persisted.

resolutions.capability: higher-level prompt discovery/trust/collision policy
resolutions.rationale: The agent-package loader is a separate lower-level implementation with no trust or collision policy. Coding-agent prompt discovery and trust belong to SET-028/003. Keep parallel-layer references; do not silently apply coding-agent behavior to the low-level helper.

resolutions.capability: coding-agent skill path discovery/hot reload and trust
resolutions.rationale: The coding-agent skill loader, refresh signature and trust path are separate from the agent-package helper. They are related integration/parallel-layer contracts, not imports required to implement this helper's exact discovery behavior.

resolutions.capability: skill invocation/list presentation
resolutions.rationale: AGENT-061 already owns model-visible invocation/list formatting. SET-031 specifies a distinct coding-agent metadata/listing path, while TUI-030 displays a parsed skill card. Rendering is a downstream concern, not a prerequisite of pure formatting.

resolutions.capability: flat custom-role JSONL codec/import/export compatibility
resolutions.rationale: The flat custom Bash message shape is input to the session codec/export. SESSION-029 already depends on AGENT-063. Preserve the type-to-codec direction and retain explicit wire adaptation rather than assuming native tagged serialization is identical.

resolutions.capability: provider-layer tool-result repair beyond this helper
resolutions.rationale: AI-014 is a later provider projection/repair with different orphan and timestamp semantics. AGENT-065 does not invoke it and must retain the separate native no-reexecution recovery stage. This is a related pipeline contract, not a prerequisite of the pure custom-role converter.

RPC-021 owns its attachment request boundary and size limits. TOOLS-020 owns shared read-path normalization, TOOLS-022 the ReadTool caller and TOOLS-023 image MIME/conversion/resize mechanics. SESSION-019 owns model-input preflight and later image policy. MISC-003 distinguishes later native user-image normalization from the CLI ingestion boundary and owns tool-result image normalization.

CLI-012 owns candidate-provider inference and request-auth extraction. AUTH-004 owns refresh/credential persistence; disabling model discovery is not a blanket network prohibition on an explicitly requested credential refresh.

AUTH-003 provides credential metadata enumeration, AUTH-004 request-auth refresh and storage preservation, AUTH-024/025 model reference/matching semantics. CLI owns only the single-value resolution policy.

AUTH owns credential schema/current store writes; SET owns literal/environment/command config resolution. Migration must not reinterpret bare uppercase strings or infer that old namespaces are aliases.

SESSION owns actual session format migration/discovery, TUI-048 pure keybinding renames, SET-003 trust decisions. This entry owns on-disk invocation, ordering, boundaries and failures; managed-tool installation is a separate MISC dependency.

SET-017 owns theme preferences and SET-018 analytics consent/tracking persistence. The package supplement owns startup theme resource resolution, and TUI-070 owns questionnaire presentation. This entry owns the caller gate and terminal lifetime.

AUTH-006 owns availability with credential metadata, AUTH-024 model reference matching, AI-002 catalog/runtime lifecycle. The actual fuzzyFilter utility is low-level TUI-owned; this entry records its key and subsequent sorting.

SET-001 owns current distribution paths, SET-005 config expression lookup and SET-010 actual settings migration. EXT-002 owns historical module aliases. Cognee/Blackhole storage users keep their existing area contracts.

OBS owns timing, recording, token/HTTP and shared-port behavior. SET-013 owns proxy/idle preferences and the HTTP dispatcher; MISC-001 owns version metadata/checks and MISC-002 Windows loaded native-dependency quarantine. RPC-020 owns JSONL shutdown/rebinding, not every CLI mode.

EXT-005 owns compatible manifest selection/entrypoint bridge. CLI-030 supplies file discovery and CLI-031 supplies pattern selection. Resource loader attribution/catalog publication remain EXT-031/SET-033 consumers.
SET-003 owns trust persistence/extension policy; SET-007/008 scoped settings. This entry owns command-specific trust call order and the stricter update policy.
The package manager and trust/parser provide operation inputs. CLI-016 is the existing selector wrapper prerequisite; TUI-068/069 are its component dependencies and should not become reverse links.

AI-002 owns ModelRuntime catalog lifecycle, network permissions, publication and cancellation. SET-001 supplies agent paths. AUTH-032 is a different startup helper and is intentionally not used as the generic refresh dependency.

CLI-027 supplies extension updates for combined targets; SET-002 chooses safe commands/install method; MISC-001 validates release metadata/comparison and MISC-002 owns loaded-DLL quarantine/cleanup. Native activation counterparts are preserved in CLI-043–046.

TOOLS-023 owns MIME, codecs, worker execution and all resize/hint algorithms. This entry owns normalization placement, default propagation, identity and failure disposition. SESSION-019 and CLI-009 retain their separate input/argument admission boundaries.

TOOLS-023 owns shared image codec/resize helpers; this entry owns clipboard acquisition and its separate converter. Root's native run.rs443–725 source credit supplies copied-file parsing/previews; TUI owns input routing and model-image settings.

AI-001/002, SESSION-018, AUTH-015 and SUB-008 own the actual retry, refresh, auth and approval integration. This entry specifies shared helper ownership and does not add their execution behavior or LOC again.

TOOLS-028/029 own observable Find/Grep search semantics and credit Rust's existing in-process traversal. RPC-022 and the TUI completion owner consume search-path availability. CLI-040/041 preserve the distinct native package/artifact installation and verification machinery; no executable installer LOC is duplicated here.

AGENT-048–054 own generic shell configuration/environment/capture/kill/cleanup algorithms. TOOLS-002 owns current-session environment and spawn hooks; TOOLS-008/010 own background cleanup/output. MISC-010 explains why native Find/Grep need no downloaded executables. Only application PATH integration and any agreed coding-wrapper compatibility correction are counted here.

Provider login and TUI presentation own when and whether a destination is offered/opened; OBS-014 owns dashboard URL/token policy. This helper owns only native launcher process/stdio behavior, not those destinations' trust or protocol semantics.

SET-001/CLI-001 resolve distribution assets. The TUI owns when startup or /changelog displays and persists a baseline; this entry owns parsing/link transformation. MISC-012 owns any eventual external link launcher, not Markdown link resolution.

TUI-201 owns the shared native width/stripping implementation and any general parser correction; TUI-202 owns terminal sequence extraction and wrapping state. MISC-011 owns the different shell binary-output sanitizer. This entry records the application helper compatibility boundary and adds no duplicate parser LOC.

SESSION/EXT own prompt, session replacement and lifecycle algorithms; RPC-017 owns raw output guarding/backpressure and shared JSON wire details, RPC-020 the runtime host contract. CLI-019 already owns caller-level harness/service cleanup. This entry counts only single-shot text behavior and its cleanup/rebinding integration, not a second runtime implementation.

RPC-017 owns JsonAgentSessionEvent mapping, raw stream guard and the live ToolUse serde mismatch; this entry owns single-shot framing/lifetime and avoids duplicating wire DTO LOC. SESSION owns lifecycle, retry/queue/compaction events. CLI-019 owns outer startup/output cleanup.

SESSION-029/030/034 own the journal schema, decoding and read views; CLI/RPC own invocation and response wrappers. TUI-004 owns resolved/export theme colors. MISC-018/019 own the browser viewer and content rendering; MISC-020 owns custom tool prerendering. Vendored library bodies and shared theme logic are not counted again as native implementation LOC.

MISC-017 supplies data/assets; MISC-019 supplies rendered content. SESSION-029/030/034 own the journal schema, tolerant reads and branch views. TUI-078 owns the concrete /share uploader and ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL; no upload mechanism or LOC is assigned to this template.

TOOLS owns execution/image normalization and AI-012 owns tool-schema validation, but historical export rendering still validates/escapes independently. MISC-020 owns standard custom-renderer HTML generation. SESSION-029/034 supply message/entry schemas and views, not browser escaping.

MISC-017 owns traversal inclusion/file output; MISC-019 consumes the resulting HTML. EXT-036 owns extension tool render callbacks, per-call state and fallback rendering; TUI-031 owns concrete TUI host presentation and is not reimplemented here. TUI-004 supplies theme colors; ANSI export conversion is separate from terminal rendering.

MISC-023 owns inference/auth/catalog publication; MISC-024 owns user decisions and progress cancellation. MISC-007/SET-013 supply shared cancellation/HTTP policy where appropriate; the router's completion state machine remains specific to this client. AI-003's generic inference dispatch does not satisfy management endpoint support.

AI-002 owns generation-safe publish/cache/runtime refresh and AI-003 compatible provider dispatch; AI-005 owns shared thinking helpers. AUTH-006/015 own generic availability/login/persistence. EXT-018 supplies provider registration. This entry adds the concrete llama provider rules without duplicating those hosts.

Router/HF/provider algorithms belong to MISC-021/022/023. TUI-048 owns keybindings, TUI-235 fuzzy matching and TUI-073 generic extension widgets. EXT owns command/custom-UI host lifetime; AUTH owns the separate login command. Only the concrete llama manager state machine and views are counted here.

CLI owns installation and invocation; AUTH owns provider credentials; RPC owns remote connection behavior; EXT-056 owns direct extension process execution and SET-003 project trust. Those runtime contracts do not become a container isolation implementation merely because documentation mentions isolation.

MISC-030 supplies local config/credentials and MISC-037 cleanup. EXT-018/013/022 own provider, command and lifecycle host contracts; AI-003 owns the provider interface. The external bridge's status/authentication claims are accepted protocol data, not independently verified billing or subscription evidence.

MISC-030 supplies endpoint/credential; MISC-032 supplies private wire identity. AI-006 owns shared request options and non-widening hard-output authority. The server's tool-context fingerprint, request validation and SDK invocation are external dependencies and unverified here.

MISC-034 supplies clean framing and MISC-033 request/tool context. AI-012 owns general tool-schema validation; this adapter's shape/name check does not replace the host's normal schema and authority checks. Server SDK behavior and tool-context correlation beyond the echoed handle are external and unverified.
MISC-034 supplies framed records and MISC-035 the validated terminal. AI-003 owns shared provider/event-stream interfaces; existing native owned partial snapshots should be retained.

MISC-030 authenticates cancellation and MISC-034 owns response reader cleanup. AI-006 supplies the shared cancellation option contract. External server TTL, disconnected-request cleanup and official SDK process termination are unverified outside these repositories.

AI-002 owns model runtime/catalog behavior; SESSION-028 owns SDK service/session construction and SESSION-035 owns resource reload. This entry adds the evaluation-specific construction and sequence policy without recounting those implementations.

The eval infrastructure entries own execution/artifacts/comparisons. Extension discovery/loading/driver and session reload remain prerequisites; this entry owns scenario inputs, output projection and correctness criteria only. Native runtime branding/path choice follows the active fork's SET-001 contract rather than mechanically creating an obsolete user directory.
